newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma approves 1997 draft budget.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma approves 1997 draft budget.

text.p: Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament approved the government's 1997 draft budget on its fourth and final reading by 245 votes to 90 and 17 absentions.
The draft now passes to the upper chamber Federation Council for consideration. It must also be signed by President Boris Yeltsin before becoming law.

The Duma, which is dominated by the communist opposition, had already approved the bulk of the spending plans, but Friday's debate went on late into the evening as lawmakers haggled over amendments to the budget.
The draft calls for a 3.5 percent budget deficit, by Russian calculations, on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles and expenditures of 529.8 trillion roubles.
Yeltsin and his government, battling a deep economic slump, will be relieved that their spending plans have finally cleared the main parliamentary hurdle after months of wrangling.

Parliament had already rejected the budget once, forcing the cash-strapped government to raise spending in certain areas, while trying to honour reform commitments made to the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The communists and their allies had been seeking additional protection for the millions of Russians who have lost out during the country's painful transition to a market economy. economic planning is coming under control.
